clue.text: Fabric for Mary's family

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Mary had a little lamb, so what belongs to Mary is the lamb's
kin are one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Someone picks out cloth for the Mary side of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Mary had a little lamb' turns 'Mary's' into LAMB'S, so 'Mary's family' is the lamb's kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambskin is the skin of a young sheep dressed with its wool on, used as a material for clothing.

clue.text: Nymph so visible in the locality

indicators.note: the word for 'so' can be seen sitting inside the word for the locality

parts.note: an area is a locality or district
thus means so, in this way

explanation.surface: A nymph is spotted in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visible in' puts THUS inside AREA, splitting it as ARE + A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arethusa is a nymph of Greek myth, changed into a spring to escape the river god Alpheus.

clue.text: Chap with diamonds, mass-murderer in sensational novel

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap
ice is slang for diamonds
a ripper is a serial killer, after Jack the Ripper

explanation.surface: A thriller plot: a man with jewels and a serial killer.
explanation.walkthrough: BOD is British slang for a chap; Jack the Ripper was the Victorian London killer behind RIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice-ripper is a lurid romantic novel with heaving passions, often historical.

clue.text: Exciting race with swimmer

parts.note: kind means race or sort, as in humankind
the ling is a fish, so a swimmer

explanation.surface: A thrilling contest against a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exciting' looks like a description of the race, but it is the definition, in the sense of stirring up feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle passions is to stir them up, so kindling here means arousing.

clue.text: Old bottles useless for this town in Wales?

definitions.text: Old bottles useless for this town in Wales?

parts.words: Old bottles useless for this town in Wales?
parts.note: alludes to the saying about not putting new wine into old bottles, here applied to a fortified wine that is fresh

explanation.surface: Old bottles are no good for some Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical warning against putting new wine in old bottles is the joke: the fresh fortified wine would need new bottles, and the town is in Monmouthshire, south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Newport is a city in south-east Wales, read as a fresh batch of the fortified wine from Portugal.

clue.text: Considered including something insignificant in dictionary

indicators.note: the dictionary's letters wrap around those of the trifle

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a pin is a trifle, as in 'not worth a pin'

explanation.surface: A lexicographer weighs whether to include a trivial entry in the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold or express a view, so opined means gave a considered opinion.

clue.text: European hero of Trollope or Twain

definitions.meaning: Trollope wrote Phineas and Twain wrote Huckleberry, each with this surname

explanation.surface: A European protagonist from a Victorian or American novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: One from Finland is a Finnish national; Phineas of Trollope's political novels and Huckleberry of Twain share the surname.

clue.text: Leaves area for putting on at Rye, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another goes after it

parts.note: a green is the area of a golf course where you putt

indicators.note: signals the letters of Rye may be shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the putting green at Rye golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges RYE into ERY, which goes on after GREEN. Rye is a town in Sussex with a well-known golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is foliage, the green leaves of plants collectively.

clue.text: Supporting framework for one in fall-back position, retreating

indicators.note: going backwards, so the whole built word is read right to left
the numeral for one goes into the word for falling back

parts.note: a relapse is a falling back into a former state
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A frame for someone who has gone back to their old position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I into RELAPSE after its RE, giving REILAPSE, and 'retreating' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a trellis on which fruit trees are trained flat against a wall.

clue.text: Paid comedian's assistant

definitions.meaning: the straight man who sets up a comic's punchlines

explanation.surface: A stooge who is paid to help a comic.
explanation.definitionFit: To fee someone is to pay them, and a feed is a stooge who supplies lines for the comic to cap.

clue.text: Mid-western city celebrated throughout the US in July

definitions.meaning: a city in Missouri near Kansas City

definitions.text: celebrated throughout the US in July
definitions.meaning: the Fourth of July holiday marks the American break from Britain

explanation.surface: A Midwestern city marks a national holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Independence, Missouri, was Truman's home town; Independence Day on 4 July is the national holiday.

clue.text: Foolishly enter with queen — is she mounted?

indicators.note: acting foolishly suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A queen enters unwisely, and someone asks whether she is on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' rearranges ENTER, QUEEN and IS together into the twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrienne is a female horse rider, so a woman in the saddle.

clue.text: Exhumer, indeed, might reveal these within

definitions.text: Exhumer, indeed, might reveal these within

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the run of the words Exhumer and indeed

explanation.surface: A gravedigger might uncover these bones.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: someone digging up a body would find these arm bones, and the run is concealed across 'Exhumer, indeed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Humeri, plural of humerus, are the upper arm bones a gravedigger might unearth.

clue.text: Increase bid showing confidence in contract

definitions.meaning: to make twice as great again
at bridge, a call doubling an opponent's double

explanation.surface: Raise a bid, confident you will make your contract.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge a player who has been doubled may redouble, raising the stakes because they expect to make the contract.
explanation.definitionFit: To redouble efforts is to intensify them; at bridge the call multiplies the scoring again.

clue.text: Proceeds to give thanks to coll-: ege

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
King's is a college at Cambridge (and at London)

explanation.surface: A college is given money as thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'college' broken across a line as 'coll-: ege'. TA is British slang for thanks; King's College, Cambridge, gives KINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the money received, the proceeds of a sale or business.

clue.text: Is it fought out without hard struggle? On the contrary

definitions.text: Is it fought out without hard struggle? On the contrary

indicators.note: out signals the letters of fought are put in disorder, with the letter for hard left over and dropped

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be shuffled
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
war is a struggle or fight

explanation.surface: A question whether a contest is won without effort, answered with a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FOUGHT and 'without' drops H (hard), leaving TUGOF; add WAR. 'On the contrary': the contest is indeed fought with hard struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug-of-war is a contest of strength between two teams pulling a rope, plainly hard struggle.

clue.text: Herb's son dividing the conference

indicators.note: the abbreviation for son splits the word for the conference in two

parts.note: a parley is a conference, especially between enemies
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A man named Herb has a son who causes rifts at the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' reads like a man's name with a son; it is the definition, and 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is a culinary plant with curly leaves, used as a garnish.

clue.text: Flying first class, king was held up

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as letter I
R is short for rex, king
borne means carried or supported, so held up

explanation.surface: A monarch travelling first class finds his flight delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' suggests delay, but BORNE means carried. A1, first class, is written AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Airborne means in the air, carried aloft, as an aircraft in flight.

clue.text: Impudent in style, turning up in warehouse

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up reads the built word from the bottom
the word for impudent goes into the word for style

parts.note: tone means manner or style
pert means cheeky or impudent

explanation.surface: Someone cheeky with style walks into a storehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PERT inside TONE, giving TOPERTNE, and 'turning up' reads that from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a trading port or depot where goods are stored before re-export.

clue.text: Vital characteristic in tonic

definitions.meaning: in music, the first note of a scale on which the key is based

explanation.surface: A tonic's key quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A keynote is the main theme of a speech, and in music the first note of a key, the tonic.

clue.text: Lead or carbon, actually

definitions.meaning: despite being called lead, the material is in fact a form of carbon

explanation.surface: Pencil lead turns out to be carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Pencil leads are made of a soft black form of carbon, which is not the metal at all.

clue.text: Pacific island's nicer resort

parts.note: I is short for island; the 's is a possessive

indicators.note: to resort the letters is to sort them again, rearranging nicer

explanation.surface: A Pacific island makes a pleasanter holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' is not the ocean but the adjective meaning peaceful; 'resort' rearranges NICER into RENIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Irenic means peaceable or conciliatory, from the Greek for peace.

clue.text: It's unusually valuable

parts.note: a thing prized because few of its kind exist

explanation.surface: Something prized for being out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is an uncommon thing, and scarceness is what makes it precious.

clue.text: Belt — Bob could have got a couple more

definitions.text: Belt — Bob could have got a couple more

parts.words: Belt — Bob could have got a couple more
parts.note: a belt is a punch; a bob, the old shilling of twelve pence, would buy three punches priced at a third of it each

explanation.surface: Someone named Bob could have taken two more blows.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'fourpenny one' is old British slang for a punch; a 'bob' was a shilling, twelve old pennies, enough for two more of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase for a clout or thump, as if a blow cost four old pence.

clue.text: State what's needed to begin upgrading the Albert Hall

indicators.note: the beginnings of the words upgrading, the, Albert and Hall are taken

explanation.surface: A request for what is needed to start renovating the Royal Albert Hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Albert Hall is the London concert venue; the opening letters of 'upgrading the Albert Hall' spell the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is a western US state whose capital is Salt Lake City.

clue.text: Calls in card game (opposite of bridge)

indicators.note: taking the word the other way round, its opposite direction

parts.note: a span is a bridge or arch across a gap

explanation.surface: Bids in a card game unlike bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' seems to be the card game, but it is SPAN, turned round by 'opposite of'. Nap is an old card game in which players call how many tricks they will take.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game nap, a bid to take all five tricks is a nap, so calls made are naps.

clue.text: In an unbalanced state, member's unable to keep calm

indicators.note: the limb sits inside the word for a tilt

parts.note: a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship
an arm is a limb or member; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A club member is too agitated to stay calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts ARM inside LIST, after A from 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist is someone who panics or spreads needless fear, failing to stay composed.

clue.text: Steelmen blended iron and carbon etc

indicators.note: mixing the letters of Steelmen as metal is blended

explanation.surface: Steel workers blend iron, carbon and other ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron and carbon are chemical substances that cannot be broken down further, examples of the kind.
